evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: UI_Command_Catalog.md is the canonical owner document for stable UI command catalog requirements and preserves product, runtime, storage, UI, and governance details in owner-section form.

items.impact: This establishes the catalog owner, stable identifier discipline, naming constraints, command-family containment, and the metadata envelope that downstream consumers must preserve.
items.statement: UCC-002 through UCC-008 coherently establish catalog ownership, compatibility vocabulary, naming, stable command IDs, family organization, and a metadata contract while explicitly avoiding executable build artifacts.
items.title: Command catalog identity and metadata baseline

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: UI command IDs are stable SSOT identifiers referenced by plans and tests; GUI labels may clean casing or spacing, but internal IDs remain stable, collision-safe, and preserve canonical command-id tokens.

items.impact: Independent builders could implement incompatible collision detection, alias-chain validation, cycle handling, or migration precedence while all claiming stable and collision-safe IDs.
items.statement: The units require stable, collision-safe IDs and preserve aliases, but this window does not define a deterministic registry-level oracle for duplicate IDs, alias cycles, multi-hop alias targets, canonical-versus-compatibility precedence, or migration-time collision adjudication.
items.title: Stable IDs lack deterministic collision and alias adjudication

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The command catalog owns command metadata and normalization intent, the route schema owns route-target structure, and wiring rows reference command IDs and handlers without restating full routing semantics.

items.impact: This creates a clear separation between catalog metadata, route structure, wiring, permission decisions, UI wrappers, and normalized command records.
items.statement: UCC-009 through UCC-015 define the route and wiring ownership boundary, permission and projection gates, route/open identity, wrapper discipline, and normalized command envelope without allowing local UI authority over protected decisions.
items.title: Routing, gating, and normalized command envelope

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Mutating domain_action commands must apply catalog-wide projection-freshness gating before dispatch, and catalog verification must cover UX flow, storage/audit, tools/permissions/provider/identity, and cross-doc routing semantics.

items.impact: A projection can become stale after the gate but before mutation, allowing dispatch under obsolete permission, identity, target, or blocked-state facts; partial side effects then have no catalog-level recovery contract.
items.statement: Projection freshness is required before dispatch, but the window does not bind freshness to an atomic revision, lease, compare-and-swap, or handler-side recheck, nor define the observable outcome when state changes between command construction, gating, and side-effect execution.
items.title: Projection freshness gate has a dispatch race

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: TierContext, tier_id, TierType, Tiers, allowed_actions[], reason_code, recovery_options[], approve_continue, and tier-era event examples are compatibility-only and current runtime approvals resolve through package/seam/lane identity and blocked-state contracts.

items.impact: The catalog prevents stale tier-era, web, artifact, runtime, and filename-shaped tokens from silently becoming active command semantics.
items.statement: UCC-016 through UCC-021 explicitly retire tier-era and stale command vocabulary, constrain artifact drill-through to shared route/open contracts, and classify uncataloged signals and extraction hazards as registration or retirement obligations.
items.title: Compatibility retirement and extraction-hazard guard

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Later-model GUI readiness requires projection-trust, gating, MVP, GUI, IDs, promoted-feature, multi-project-tab, attention-center, runtime cmd.runtime.* ownership, and cross-doc command-family gaps to resolve to catalog rows or owner retirements.

items.impact: Build readiness can be declared inconsistently because an uncataloged caller, ghost ID, or unresolved owner retirement may remain outside the checked set.
items.statement: The units name broad readiness gaps and require catalog rows or owner retirements, but this window provides no closed-world manifest that enumerates every expected caller, command ID, alias, retirement record, owner, and machine-checkable closure result.
items.title: Readiness blockers are not closed-world enumerable

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Wiring_Matrix.schema.json stays lean by pointing to catalog and route/open contracts, while usage and artifact summary drift remains a consumer/owner gap rather than a command payload shape.

items.impact: This avoids duplicated payload schemas and keeps graph, route, history, operational identity, and shell-view consumers from minting local command contracts.
items.statement: UCC-022 through UCC-027 preserve lean wiring, bind HITL/runtime governance to owner contracts, constrain graph and object routing, and keep operational identity and shell-view schemas with their owning documents.
items.title: Lean wiring and cross-surface owner boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Ledger export, show-in commands, operational identity displays, runtime-artifact/worktree/account owner schemas, route ID discipline, blocked runtime identity tuples, UICommand args, and Crosswalk primitives preserve owner boundaries rather than local schema ownership.

items.impact: Consumers can agree that ownership is external yet bind to different owner schemas, versions, or identifiers, producing cross-document divergence that local validation cannot falsify.
items.statement: The window repeatedly says to preserve external owner boundaries but does not provide a normative resolution table mapping each named identity, tuple, wrapper, and schema field to one owner anchor, contract version, consumer obligation, and validation oracle.
items.title: Cross-document owner claims lack a resolvable mapping

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Every catalog command must be verifiable through the Wiring Matrix with handler registration, event-emission tests when events are declared, UI element binding, and testable acceptance_checks; commands with no persisted domain event remain subject to handler and UI binding checks.

items.impact: The window binds catalog commands to wiring verification and defines concrete GitHub auth, project, file-manager, and LSP families with arguments, events, and surfaces.
items.statement: UCC-028 through UCC-034 establish wiring acceptance hooks and concrete command families for GitHub authentication, project creation, file management, and LSP integration.
items.title: Wiring verification and foundational command families

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: cmd.github.connect starts a fresh GitHub OAuth device-code flow with empty args locked by Spec Lock, emits device-code/polling/authenticated-or-failed events, affects GitHub/Auth setup surfaces, and uses recovery wrappers with keyed context for deferred reconnect.

items.impact: Concurrent connects, expired device codes, offline polling, late authentication after disconnect, token deletion failure, or provider-side revocation failure can leave misleading UI state or retained credentials without a deterministic recovery or audit outcome.
items.statement: The GitHub auth rows specify happy-path events and token deletion but do not define device-code expiry and cancellation, polling backoff and network loss, concurrent-flow supersession, disconnect-versus-poll races, provider revocation, credential-store partial failure, or the authoritative reconciliation oracle for UI auth state.
items.title: GitHub authentication lifecycle is under-specified

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The minimum LSP command ID list includes goto definition, find references, rename symbol, format document/selection, code action, goto symbol, open problems, and restart server commands with their args.

items.impact: This defines stable LSP and layout capabilities, normalizes graph recovery into runtime ownership, introduces Orchestrator route wrappers, and reserves operational namespaces from replacement.
items.statement: UCC-035 through UCC-041 define LSP and widget commands, runtime recovery normalization, Orchestrator wrappers and metadata, external-system boundaries, and reserved first-party namespaces with compatibility aliases.
items.title: LSP, layout, runtime wrappers, and namespace reservations

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Operational namespaces reserve Source Control, git worktree, GitHub Actions, Docker, Docker Kubernetes, Kubernetes compatibility aliases, and core first-party prefixes against plugin/custom override while preserving explicit extension verbs.

items.impact: Plugins, migrations, and built-ins can disagree about whether an ID is an allowed extension, forbidden override, compatibility alias, or canonical owner, creating nondeterministic dispatch and authority capture.
items.statement: Reserved namespaces and explicit extension verbs are required, but the window does not define the extension-verb grammar, registration authority, canonicalization order, alias-versus-plugin precedence, conflict diagnostics, or a machine-checkable rejection oracle.
items.title: Reserved namespace extension precedence is ambiguous

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Operational command coverage must include Source Control navigation/history/graph/worktrees/git operations, GitHub Actions rerun/cancel/pin/admin/current-branch/log pivots, Docker Manager images/compose/bake/context/network/volume/Kubernetes/auth/publish/remediation families, and deterministic disabled-state/help behavior.

items.impact: The plan recognizes full operational breadth, persistent owner surfaces, stable review and conflict commands, graph/history assistance, and concrete disabled-state behavior.
items.statement: UCC-042 through UCC-047 require broad operational coverage and define route persistence, Source Control review/conflict/graph/history commands, compare-state boundaries, and GitHub Actions run/job/log pivots.
items.title: Operational coverage and Source Control workflows

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Source Control review, conflict, merge editor, git diff, hunk staging, discard, and conflict resolution command rows define stable command IDs, payloads, confirmations, and preconditions for review and conflict workflows.

items.impact: Concurrent repository changes or partial git failures can make staged, discarded, resolved, or compared state differ from what the UI confirmed, with no deterministic rollback, refresh, or receipt requirement in this window.
items.statement: The catalog asserts payloads, confirmations, preconditions, persistence, and disabled states, but does not specify repository revision guards, dirty-worktree races, idempotency, partial hunk application outcomes, rollback limits, stale-diff invalidation, or observable receipts for destructive Source Control actions.
items.title: Destructive Source Control commands lack race and rollback semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: GitHub Actions commands carry workflow/run/job/step/check/log identity for route-open pivots, preserve source-control correlation, and treat legacy cmd.github_actions.* and cmd.actions pin/unpin names as compatibility aliases rather than a second namespace.

items.impact: The plan preserves correlated GitHub Actions identity and defines Docker build, compose, registry, Kubernetes, disabled-state, approval, and receipt-lineage requirements while retiring duplicate namespaces.
items.statement: UCC-048 through UCC-053 define GitHub Actions correlation and aliases plus Docker build, compose, registry, Kubernetes, approval, availability, and receipt-lineage command semantics.
items.title: GitHub Actions correlation and Docker/Kubernetes command families

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Docker/Kubernetes availability copy uses shared disabled-state taxonomy from runtime projection state, side effects use domain-bound approval scoping, receipts retain docker_refs and kubernetes_refs lineage, and drift/trust blockers refresh effective capability before mutation.

items.impact: Retries, network partitions, context drift, partial multi-resource operations, or approval reuse can mutate the wrong registry, cluster, namespace, workload, or tag while producing incomplete lineage and misleading recovery state.
items.statement: The Docker/Kubernetes units require approval scoping, capability refresh, and lineage receipts, but this window does not define idempotency keys, approval binding fields and expiry, target revision checks, retry classification, partial-success receipts, compensating actions, rollback limits, or reconciliation after network loss.
items.title: Docker and Kubernetes mutations lack transaction semantics

segments.summary: Reviewed owner identity, compatibility vocabulary, naming, stable IDs, command-family organization, metadata, and adversarial collision and alias behavior.
Reviewed route and wiring boundaries, availability gates, projection freshness, route/open identity, wrappers, normalization, and dispatch-race failure modes.
Reviewed compatibility retirement, stale command guards, artifact routing, GUI readiness blockers, uncataloged signals, and closed-world coverage risk.
Reviewed lean wiring, HITL/runtime ownership, graph and object routes, operational identity, shell-view lineage, and resolvability of cross-document owner claims.
Reviewed wiring acceptance hooks, GitHub auth, project, file-manager, and LSP contracts plus authentication lifecycle, privacy, race, and recovery behavior.
Reviewed LSP, widget layout, runtime recovery normalization, Orchestrator wrappers, external-system families, reserved namespaces, and extension precedence.
Reviewed operational breadth, persistence, Source Control review/conflict/graph/history, GitHub Actions pivots, and destructive-action concurrency and rollback gaps.
Reviewed GitHub Actions correlation and aliases, Docker build/compose/registry/Kubernetes families, disabled states, approvals, receipts, and external-mutation transaction gaps.
